why: The Pima County moratorium applies only to unincorporated areas per its scope parameter, and the site is inside Tucson city, so the moratorium does not apply. The 300 MW project assumes N+1 diesel generators of 2500 kW each (121 units total) with 500 h/yr emergency-engine PTE and 6.4 g/kWh NOx (Tier 2 diesel), yielding an estimated NOx potential to emit of 1,067 tpy. This exceeds the 100 tpy major-source threshold under 40 CFR 70.2, triggering a federal Title V operating permit requirement. The Title V permit is a major permitting constraint that adds cost and time but does not block the project outright. Therefore, the project can proceed conditionally upon securing the Title V permit.

Pima County passes 120-day moratorium on future data center projects
Board of Supervisors adopted a 120-day moratorium on new data center permit applications in unincorporated Pima County while the county finalizes a data-center zoning code amendment.
Pima County passes 120-day moratorium on future data center projects

Active as of 2026-09-23. 120-day moratorium on the acceptance/issuance of new data center permits in unincorporated Pima County, adopted 3-2 (Supervisors Christy and Scott dissenting) on 2026-08-11 and running to approximately 2026-12-09, while Development Services finalizes a zoning code text amendment. The department is seeking public comment (online survey; a September 28, 2026 open house; proposed rules going to the Planning and Zoning Commission on October 28, 2026) on a related, permanent zoning code amendment that would define data centers (facilities using more than 20 MW), require closed-loop cooling, and set review/design standards; that permanent amendment is expected in December 2026, around when the moratorium runs out.

It suspends eligibility for the incentive; it does not pause data center construction, siting, or local permitting.
